summary: Data dir, node.id, lock and holder wiring with nodedir and ulid
change: After loading settings, call `d, err := nodedir.Open(s.DataDir)`, which creates root, identity/ and lkg/ with mode 0700 and refuses a non-directory, a directory not owned by the euid, or a world-writable one. Then call `id, err := d.NodeID(func() (ulid.ULID, error) { return ulid.New(clk.Now(), nil) })`, which reads or creates identity/node-id once; nil entropy means crypto/rand. Next call `lk, err := d.TryLock()`: errors.Is(err, nodedir.ErrLocked) means a live holder, so take the handover successor path on Linux (WP-89) or exit 1 with 'data dir in use' elsewhere; errors.ErrUnsupported means a platform without flock. As holder, call `h, herr := nodedir.NewHolder(id, buildinfo.Get().Version)`, log herr if set (the record is still returned), then call `lk.WriteHolder(h)`. Keep the *nodedir.Lock reachable for the process lifetime: store it in the supervisor and hand it to drain and lkg, because a garbage-collected Lock closes its file and drops the flock. The Drain's lk.Release() also removes holder.json.

summary: Write and remove lkg/ files only through Lock.WriteFile and Lock.Remove
change: Write and delete every file under lkg/ (content, pointers, candidate) only through the holder's *nodedir.Lock. `lk.WriteFile("lkg/<name>", data)` writes atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, fsync of the directory) with mode 0600 and refuses lock, holder.json and identity/node-id. `lk.Remove("lkg/<name>")` treats a missing file as success. Both fail with nodedir.ErrReleased once the Drain (WP-67) has called Lock.Release at Drain start, and Release waits for an in-flight write, so no LKG write can follow the release (spec 04 req 7). Treat ErrReleased as 'stop writing': no retry and no lkg_write_failed. A handover successor holds no Lock and writes nothing under lkg/ until it takes the lock; reads may use Dir.LKGPath().

summary: State in the Store contract that Get publishes a poll's values before watchers run and keeps them on watcher failure
change: Extend the secret.Store doc comments in internal/secret/secret.go (doc only). Get returns a new value as soon as the resolver publishes it. Within one poll the resolver publishes every changed reference of the active Store before it calls any watcher, so fn can Get the other half of a pair and see this poll's value. A watcher's error or panic never withdraws a published value: Get keeps returning it, and only that watcher keeps its last value and counts a failure. A file value that fails a use check of the active Store is never published: Get keeps the last good value and secret_rotation_failed is raised. summary: jsonval *Object index cost and read-only sharing rules for consumers
change: An *Object with more than 8 members keeps a name index that Decode, Clone and every mutation maintain. summary: Create secret files 0600/0644 in quickstart and Compose; no owner allow-list setting
change: WP-53 (examples/quickstart, the examples/file-mode README) and WP-95 (Compose suite with bind-mounted secrets): create secret files with an explicit mode 0600 or 0644 (chmod or install -m), never relying on umask. On hosts with umask 002 new files are 0664, and the resolver refuses any file writable by group or others with RZ-CFG-026. Any owner is accepted, so Compose bind mounts resolve whatever their host UID. WP-76: leave resolver.Config.FileOwners empty, and do not add a RURALZ_* owner allow-list setting: no document defines one, and inventing settings is forbidden. If it is ever needed, propose it through an Open questions row.

summary: Redis driver uses the resolver's literal loopback rule
change: WP-41: the credentials check in redis URL validation and the state_store_unauthenticated degraded reason (spec 08 req 8) must use the same literal loopback rule as internal/secret/resolver/check.go:275-285 (isLoopbackLiteral). Loopback means `localhost` in any case, an IPv4 literal in 127.0.0.0/8, or ::1. IPv4-mapped forms such as ::ffff:127.0.0.1 are not loopback, even though netip's IsLoopback counts them, and DNS results never count. Apply the rule to the URL host and to every `addr` query host. The redis row cannot import secret/resolver, so implement an identical function and reuse the resolver's test table.

summary: filterClass: R-7 materializes it on every Policy; CheckFilterClass is the only rule
change: WP-37 (stage G defaults and convert) and WP-56 (stage H validate): architecture R-7 overrides 01 J 39's RZ-CFG-005 row ('filterClass only for plugin') and 01 note 9. The registry materializes spec.filterClass on every Policy, so neither stage may reject a non-plugin Policy whose authored filterClass restates its registry class. registry.Registry.CheckFilterClass (internal/config/registry/policy.go:150-165) is the only filterClass rule. It reports RZ-CFG-005 for a differing value on a non-plugin type, or a non-class value on plugin. Call it once per Policy at stage H (WP-56) and add the source Location to its diagnostic, which carries Resource, Path and Message. Add no other filterClass check in defaults, convert or validate.

summary: Registry.Phases needs the CEL body oracle and correctly typed Config
change: Callers of registry.Registry.Phases (WP-38 precedence, WP-56 validate, WP-59 authz.cel Factory) and WP-69, which injects the oracle into precedence, must follow two rules. First, Phases fails with registry.ErrNoBodyOracle when an authz.cel Policy has a non-empty config.rule and the BodyOracle argument is nil. Pass the CEL compiler, the expr.Compiler value that internal/cel implements, which has ReferencesRequestBody, on every Phases call that can see authz.cel, and never nil in a binary. Second, Phases rejects an Attachment.Config whose type is not the Policy type's config type, for every type and before the scope rule. Pass hub.Resource.Config exactly as stage G decoded it (the registry's NewConfig pointer type, such as *v1alpha1.AuthzCELConfig), or nil.
